name: Ironblood Pact Colorblock Territory Jacket
description: A heavyweight salvage-canvas jacket cut wide at the shoulders, paneled in the Ironblood Collective's signature burnt-orange and raw-iron grey. Back panel carries a hand-pressed gang sigil in cracked rubber ink — a stylized gear split by a lightning bolt — surrounded by district patch clusters stitched in layered embroidery. Sleeve seams are deliberately split and re-laced with steel-braid cord, marking a member who has survived at least one territorial confrontation. Interior lining is mismatched salvage fabric, each piece sourced from a different dead corponation uniform.
functionality: Reinforced back panel absorbs minor impact. Laced sleeve seams can be quickly torn open to accommodate chrome arm augmentations during conflict. Interior pockets are heat-sealed for acid rain resistance.
what_it_says: This wearer belongs somewhere, and crossing them means crossing everyone who wears this color.
worn_by: the Gray Zone territorial gang affiliates
ex-members who kept the jacket anyway
price_range: Φ0 (earned, not purchased) — black market Φ180–Φ400
story_hooks: A runner finds a dead Ironblood member's jacket — wearing it could open doors or get them killed depending on which district they're in.
A corponation intelligence analyst has been tasked with mapping gang patch genealogy to predict territorial shifts — she needs a jacket to go undercover.
Someone is selling authenticated Ironblood jackets to Tier 4 fashion tourists, and the Collective has noticed.

physical_description.visual_profile: A imposing, wide-shouldered silhouette that reads aggressive and territorial. The burnt-orange and raw-iron grey colorblock creates stark visual division across the torso and sleeves. The jacket commands presence—not sleek, but deliberately heavy and unmissable. Instantly identifiable as Ironblood Collective affiliated.
physical_description.fit: Deliberately oversized through shoulders and chest, relaxed through the body. Cut to allow layering and movement for street conflict. Sleeves are slightly cropped, exposing the re-laced seams intentionally.
physical_description.primary_material: Salvage-canvas—heavy, treated cotton-blend composite from decommissioned industrial textiles. Durable enough for repeated wear and impact resistance. Steel-braid cord for re-lacing.
physical_description.texture: Rough, tactile canvas with visible weave. Hand-pressed rubber ink on back panel is slightly raised and cracked from age/use, creating depth. Embroidered district patches add layered dimension. Steel-braid cord seams are rigid and industrial.
physical_description.color_scheme: Burnt-orange (primary) and raw-iron grey (secondary) in bold colorblock panels. Black cracked-rubber ink for gang sigil. Mismatched interior linings visible at lapels and cuffs—faded corporate blues, greys, and blacks creating visual texture.
physical_description.closures: Heavy brass or salvage-metal zipper running full length. Magnetic snap collar closures. Friction-fit cuff adjustment with steel-braid lacing.
distinctive_features: Hand-pressed gang sigil (gear split by lightning bolt) on back panel in deliberately cracked rubber ink
Layered embroidered district patch clusters surrounding back sigil
Split and re-laced sleeve seams with steel-braid cord—visible marker of territorial survival
Mismatched salvage corporate uniform fragments as interior lining (each piece from different defunct corpo)
Wide shoulder construction emphasizing intimidating silhouette
Wear patterns consistent with street use and repeated conflict exposure
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 5 salvage / Tier 4 street—hand-made from scavenged materials, but culturally significant enough to signal serious gang affiliation rather than poverty
physical_description.cultural_context: Ironblood Collective member. Wearer is claimed territory, marked as survivor of territorial confrontation, and embedded in a specific district ecosystem. Signals rejection of corpo hierarchy and commitment to autonomous collective identity. Not worn casually—this is a declaration.
physical_description.condition_typical: Deliberately worn and weathered. Patches show visible stitching and age. Rubber ink intentionally cracked for aesthetic and authenticity. Brass hardware shows patina. Canvas is stiff but softened by use. Never pristine—condition communicates real street time.
